summary: 14-day Nightscout telemetry analysis reveals exceptional glycemic control with 99.7% Time in Range (70-180 mg/dL), 0.0% Time Below Range (<70 mg/dL), and a Coefficient of Variation of 12.9%. Core profile settings (basal, CR, ISF, DIA) and AAPS automation settings are well-calibrated. The primary area for minor optimization is postprandial peak blunting during weekend brunch meals through prebolus timing.

analysis_steps.findings: Data quality is excellent across 14 full days (1,345 valid entries, 100% coverage, 0 gaps >15 minutes). Telemetry and active profile data are fully complete.
analysis_steps.data_gaps: 15-minute sensor reading cadence requires evaluating trends over multi-hour windows.

analysis_steps.findings: Outstanding glycemic safety with zero hypoglycemia recorded (<70 mg/dL: 0.0%) and negligible hyperglycemia (>180 mg/dL: 0.3%). Overall variability is very low (CV 12.9%).
analysis_steps.evidence: Average glucose 117.0 mg/dL, SD 15.1 mg/dL, TIR 99.7%, TBR 0.0%. Overnight nadirs remained at or above 70 mg/dL.

analysis_steps.findings: Basal segments maintain stable glucose overnight (mean 102-107 mg/dL between 00:00 and 05:00) and throughout fasting daytime periods.
analysis_steps.evidence: Hourly local mean glucose remains tightly bounded between 102.3 mg/dL and 119.9 mg/dL in non-meal windows.
analysis_steps.data_gaps: Automated SMB and temp basal corrections obscure unlooped fasting basal drift.

analysis_steps.findings: Carbohydrate ratios (10-12 g/U), ISF (40-48 mg/dL/U), and DIA (5.5 h) are accurately calibrated, consistently returning glucose to baseline 240-360 minutes post-meal.
analysis_steps.evidence: Therapy response windows show 240m glucose changes returning to within -11 to +8 mg/dL of start values across all meal types.

analysis_steps.findings: SMB and UAM automation settings operate safely, providing effective postprandial micro-dosing without triggering insulin stacking or late drops.
analysis_steps.data_gaps: Specific boolean SMB activation toggles are null in the profile summary object.

analysis_steps.findings: Safety limits (max basal 2.4 U/h, max IOB 8.0 U) and Dynamic ISF factor (100%) provide appropriate headroom and protection.
analysis_steps.evidence: max_basal_u_per_hour = 2.4 U/h relative to max programmed basal of 1.05 U/h.
analysis_steps.data_gaps: Autosens configuration flags are unpopulated in exported JSON summary.

analysis_steps.findings: Weekday breakfast strategy (20 min prebolus, 70% immediate) achieves excellent control. Weekend brunch (10 min prebolus, 60% immediate) experiences higher 120m peaks (up to 188 mg/dL).
analysis_steps.evidence: Breakfast 120m peak +33 to +57 mg/dL; Brunch 120m peak +62 to +70 mg/dL.

analysis_steps.findings: Declared e-carbs (20g over 120m starting +15m) for weekend brunch effectively match extended fat/protein absorption, preventing late postprandial hypoglycemia.
analysis_steps.evidence: Brunch 360m glucose changes remain within -15 to -5 mg/dL of starting baseline.

analysis_steps.findings: All analysis stages demonstrate that core profile settings and AAPS loop automation are performing optimally. No profile parameter changes are recommended. Prebolus timing adjustment is suggested for weekend brunches.
analysis_steps.evidence: 99.7% TIR, 0.0% TBR, 12.9% CV across 14 full days of complete data.

strengths: Exceptional Time in Range of 99.7% (70-180 mg/dL) over 14 days.
Zero time below range (<70 mg/dL: 0.0%), demonstrating excellent safety.
Low glucose variability with a Coefficient of Variation (CV) of 12.9%.
Accurately calibrated basal rates, carb ratios, and ISF segments across all time blocks.
100% CGM data coverage with zero gaps greater than 15 minutes.
issues: Mild postprandial glucose excursions up to 188 mg/dL following weekend brunch meals due to a shorter 10-minute prebolus window.

recommendations.title: Optimize prebolus timing for weekend brunch
recommendations.description: Weekend brunch meals currently produce a 120-minute postprandial rise up to 188 mg/dL before returning to baseline. Extending the prebolus timing from 10 minutes to 15-20 minutes will help blunt this peak without altering total insulin dosing.

profile_recommendation.rationale: The current profile parameters deliver exceptional outcomes (99.7% TIR, 0% hypo, 12.9% CV) across 14 days, confirming accurate calibration of basal, CR, ISF, and DIA.
profile_recommendation.next_check: Re-evaluate postprandial peaks after testing a 15-20 minute prebolus window for weekend brunches.

implementation_steps: Confirm that core profile settings (basal rates, CR, ISF, DIA) remain unchanged.
Verify AAPS interface toggles directly on the device for completeness.
For weekend brunch meals, test extending the prebolus timing from 10 minutes to 15-20 minutes while maintaining the 60% immediate / 20g e-carb entry.
Monitor glucose postprandial trends over 3-5 weekend brunch meals to confirm peak blunting.

meal_strategy_summary.suggestion: Maintain active CR segments and AAPS UAM/SMB settings. Continue using a 20-minute prebolus with 70% immediate bolus for fast-carbohydrate meals like weekday breakfast, and combine a 15 to 20 minute prebolus with 60% immediate bolus and 20g extended carbs (e-carbs) over 120 minutes for high-fat/mixed meals like weekend brunch.
meal_strategy_summary.rationale: Postprandial glucose returns reliably to baseline across all meal types by 240-360 minutes without hypoglycemia, confirming total insulin dosing is well-calibrated.
meal_strategy_summary.next_observation: Observe whether extending Weekend Brunch prebolus to 15-20 minutes reduces the 120-minute glucose peak below 160 mg/dL without causing early dips within 60 minutes.

exceptions.suggestion: Increase prebolus time from 10 minutes to 15-20 minutes or shift immediate bolus from 60% to 70% when starting above 110 mg/dL.
exceptions.rationale: Blunts the peak excursion to 188 mg/dL while relying on declared 20g e-carbs and AAPS UAM to prevent late-tail hypoglycemia.

education: Prebolus timing synchronization helps align peak insulin action with carbohydrate absorption curves, reducing peak postprandial glucose without increasing total insulin dose.
Extended carbohydrates (e-carbs) in AAPS inform the algorithm of slow-absorbing fat and protein, enabling UAM/SMBs to safely distribute insulin over several hours.
safety_notes: Decision-support content only. The user must independently verify every proposed change with their clinical care team.
Make adjustments one at a time and monitor blood glucose closely following any strategy change.
Do not alter insulin pump parameters or loop safety limits automatically.
